name: Abyssal Plague Swarm

alignment.name: Chaotic Evil
alignment.description:
Chaotic evil creatures have a complete disregard for others. They kill, steal, and betray others to gain power. Their word is meaningless and their actions destructive. Their worldviews can be so warped that they destroy anything and anyone that doesn’t directly contribute to their interests.
	By the standards of good and lawful good people, chaotic evil is as abhorrent as evil, perhaps even more so. Chaotic evil monsters such as demons and orcs are at least as much of a threat to civilization and general well-being as evil monsters are. An evil creature and a chaotic evil creature are both opposed to good, but they don’t have much respect for each other either and rarely cooperate toward common goals.
	For the purpose of game effects, a chaotic evil creature is also considered evil.

resistances.name: half
resistances.details: damage from melee and ranged attacks

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Frenzied Swarm
traits.details: Any enemy that ends its turn in the aura takes 10 necrotic and psychic damage.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.details: The swarm can occupy the same space as another creature, and an enemy can enter its space, which is difficult terrain. The swarm cannot be pulled, pushed, or slid by melee or ranged attacks. It can squeeze through any opening that is large enough for a Tiny creature.

auras.name: Frenzied Swarm
auras.details: Any enemy that ends its turn in the aura takes 10 necrotic and psychic damage.

effect.description: Before or after the attack, the swarm shifts up to 2 squares.

powers.name: Infestation
powers.description: The target takes ongoing 5 psychic damage and is dazed (save ends both). At the end of the encounter, the target makes a saving throw. On a failure, the target contracts greater Abyssal plague (stage 1).

hit.description: psychic damage, and the target is dominated (save ends). The swarm is then removed from play. When the domination ends, the swarm reappears in an unoccupied square adjacent to the target, or in the nearest unoccupied square if that one is occupied.
